HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures ranking within a 100-item candidate set; it does not establish full-catalog HR@10. Krichene and Rendle show that sampled metrics can reverse recommender comparisons even in expectation. Keep the pinned benchmark unchanged, describe gains explicitly as sampled-candidate validation gains, and retain identical users and candidates for paired comparisons. [On Sampled Metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

Suggested uncertainty analysis: retain each model’s per-user hit indicator; compute paired differences, then resample user pairs with replacement separately within each category, preserving 200 observations/category. For each bootstrap replicate, average differences within categories and then equally across all four categories; report the observed macro difference and a 95% percentile interval. Pairing preserves dependence between models evaluated on the same users; category stratification preserves the benchmark’s macro weighting. This resamples evaluation outcomes, requiring no retraining or additional training seeds. [SciPy bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)

Repeated checkpoint/hyperparameter selection on the same validation users introduces selection optimism. A bootstrap interval computed after choosing the winner does not correct that adaptive selection or provide an unbiased confirmatory superiority claim. Label it exploratory and conditional on the fitted models and fixed candidate sets; it excludes training-seed and negative-sampling variability. Report search breadth and checkpoint-selection rules, show category-level differences, and reserve confirmation for the host’s untouched held-out evaluation after selection is frozen. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
